Forecast Discussion

3"-5" of rain is the common total across the region this morning; however, the eastern escarpment has more. Some spots will reach 8". Check out the Archive tab for our stations, and you’ll see the totals.

The remnant of Isaias is over middle Tennessee this morning and moves northeast into southern West Virginia this afternoon. From there it turns sharply east and reaches the Mid-Atlantic coast near New Jersey by Monday morning. An associated front is sweeping through from the SW this morning.

We have one more strong band of rain, with thunder, early this morning associated with the front. Then we have a brief break, but this afternoon scattered showers develop along the western escarpment. Those showers continue tonight and taper off Monday morning, with less toward the east.

The pressure difference between Isaias’s remnant to our northeast and strong high pressure to our southwest puts us in a windy northwest flow tonight into Monday.

The high to our SW builds on Tuesday and Wednesday, pushing temperatures to near-record highs by Wednesday.

A front approaches early Thursday but is repelled back to the north quickly. Warm weather continues but not near record levels. I cannot rule out a stray shower Thursday afternoon as the front moves north as a warm front.

A more important front arrives Friday with scattered showers. Behind that front is significantly cooler air, and our first widespread frost is possible Saturday night or Sunday.
